activities.caption: fill the blanks — redshift to stretch factor
activities.name: czRedshiftCloze

config.text: A Lyman-α line emitted at 121.6 nm and observed at 486 nm gives z ≈ %%0%% — the universe has stretched by a factor of %%1%% since that light left. Hubble's law reads v = %%2%% × d, with H₀ ≈ 70 km/s per megaparsec.
config.hint: 486 ÷ 121.6 − 1, the scale factor, and the constant the two independent measurements disagree about.

activities.anchor: nothing is moving through space faster than light
activities.caption: bet first — redshift 14 and the speed of light
activities.name: czDopplerPredict

config.q: JWST-era galaxies have redshifts above 14 — recession 'speeds' exceeding c. Is that a relativity violation?
choices: No — nothing moves through space faster than light; space itself stretches
Yes — relativity breaks down at cosmological scales
Only for galaxies heavier than the Milky Way
config.why: Doppler is motion through space; cosmological redshift is the stretching of wavelength by the expansion of space during transit — for distant galaxies they diverge.

activities.anchor: the most common size-of-the-universe error in popular writing
activities.caption: pair each quantity with its measured value
activities.name: czSizeMatch

config.prompt: Three different quantities in an expanding universe — match them:

pairs.right: 13.8 billion years — checked against the oldest globular-cluster stars
flat — total density equals critical to within half a per cent

pairs.left: the matter that emitted today's CMB

config.why: Distance 'then', distance 'now' and light-travel time are three different quantities — conflating them is the classic error.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the size question
activities.name: czSizeSpot

config.prompt: One line of this size answer is wrong — click it:
lines: The light from the CMB took 13.8 billion years to arrive.
The emitting region has been receding and stretching all the while.
The matter that emitted today's CMB is now about 46 billion light-years away.
The observable universe is a wall we could eventually reach, 93 billion light-years across.
config.correction: The edge of visibility, not a wall — nothing can reach beyond the cosmic horizon.
config.why: The edge of visibility is not a destination: it is where the stretching outruns the light, forever.

activities.anchor: That is why the Big Bang is consensus and not narrative
activities.caption: file the three streams — whose physics?
activities.name: czStreamsBuckets

config.prompt: Three evidence streams on three independent physics — file each:

items.label: the expansion itself — running it backward demands a hot dense beginning
the CMB, cooled to 2.7255 K, uniform to one part in 100,000
nucleosynthesis: ~75% hydrogen, ~25% helium in the first three minutes
the dipole — our 370 km/s motion against the cosmic rest frame

config.why: Galaxy dynamics, photon gas thermodynamics, nuclear reaction networks — they fail separately or not at all.

activities.anchor: where the model's six parameters come from
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the dipole speedometer
activities.name: czDipoleEstimate

config.prompt: The CMB's dipole — a part-in-a-thousand warm/cool split across the sky — is our motion against the cosmic rest frame. Roughly how many km/s is that motion?
config.why: 370 km/s — the Solar System's speedometer written in light.
config.context: The CMB's spectrum is a near-perfect black body, the most precise such measurement made in nature.

activities.anchor: tentative DESI hints (2024–25) that it may evolve
activities.caption: bet first — measure w, and the fate follows
activities.name: czFatePredict

config.q: Measure w — the pressure-to-density ratio of the dark component — and the fate follows. What fate does a constant w ≈ −1 predict?
choices: Expansion accelerates forever, fading toward a cold dilute equilibrium — the heat death
A Big Rip tearing galaxies, stars and atoms apart
config.why: A strengthening dark component would rip; a decaying one would recollapse — with w ≈ −1 constant, the current best estimate is the heat death.

activities.anchor: the residuals are where the live research lives
activities.caption: pair each component with its measured share
activities.name: czInventoryMatch

config.prompt: ΛCDM's inventory — every percentage measured, two of them unexplained:

pairs.right: ~27% — required, not optional, in any model fitting the data
~68% — the component whose constant density makes expansion accelerate

config.why: The expert habit: every claim is a fit to data, and the residuals are where the live research lives.
